sentences.text: Her name is Sara and she was twelve and she was standing on the track about four hundred metres down the Fonte side with a phone in her hand, and she had been following the same tracks up.
They looked at each other for a while.
He has thought about that pause a great deal and he does not think either of them was frightened.

What they were doing was arithmetic: two children on a track that neither village used, each working out which village the other was from and what that was supposed to mean, and both of them arriving at *I have no idea what I am supposed to do here* at about the same moment.

What Dario says about that moment, at twenty-four, is that he knew exactly who she was before she said anything, because there are two families in Fonte with that hair and one of them is the family from the court case.
Neither of them said hello.

What Sara said, eventually, holding up the phone, was: "Have you got her on anything?" And Dario said no, and that his was a rubbish phone, and that she had gone past his uncle's shed at about half five.
Sara said that she had her going up past the chapel at twenty past six.

And the two of them stood on a mule track that neither village had used since 1974 and worked out, from two sightings fifty minutes apart, roughly how fast a wolf walks, which is about four kilometres an hour, which is a fact Dario has never forgotten and has never needed.
They did that for two winters.
Not often.
Perhaps nine or ten times a year, in the snow, when the tracking was good, always on the track, always by accident to begin with and then, from about the second January, not by accident at all.
They did not become friends exactly.
Dario wants to be precise about this because the story gets away from him otherwise.

They were two children in different schools in different valleys who had one subject in common, and the subject was an animal, and they talked about the animal for a couple of hours a winter for two years and about almost nothing else.
They had no way to contact each other.

That is a detail people find hard to believe now and it is central: neither of them ever gave the other a number, for two years, because the number would have had to be explained at some point to somebody.
So it worked like this.
If it snowed, and the tracks were on the Colle side, Dario went up.
If it snowed, and she could get out, Sara went up.
Roughly a third of the time the other one was there.
He knows that her grandmother was in the 1974 meetings.
She knows that his grandfather was.
Neither of them ever raised it and Dario cannot now remember which of them decided that.
